steps.title: Python for ML
steps.subtitle: Write clean, data-ready Python
steps.description: Get fluent in the Python you will use every day as an ML engineer: core syntax, built-in data structures, OOP and fast NumPy arrays. You also set up a reproducible workflow with virtual environments, Jupyter and Git that every later step builds on.

topics.name: Python fundamentals: variables, control flow, functions and list/dict comprehensions
Built-in data structures: list, tuple, dict and set, and when to use each
Object-oriented Python: classes, __init__, inheritance, class vs instance attributes
Files, exceptions, modules and memory-friendly iteration with generators
NumPy arrays: shapes, indexing/slicing (views vs copies), broadcasting and vectorization
Reproducible setup: virtual environments, pip + requirements.txt, Git commits and GitHub
Jupyter / Google Colab workflow, including Restart & Run All to avoid hidden state

steps.title: Data Handling, Math & Statistics
steps.subtitle: Clean, query and understand your data
steps.description: Real ML work is mostly data work. Learn to load, clean and reshape data with Pandas, query it with SQL and explore it visually, and build the probability, statistics and linear-algebra intuition that every model relies on.

topics.name: Pandas DataFrames: read_csv, selecting, filtering, groupby and merge
Data cleaning: missing values, duplicates, outliers and wrong data types
Preprocessing: categorical encoding (one-hot/label) and feature scaling (standardization, min-max)
SQL for data: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY/HAVING and window functions
Probability & statistics: distributions, mean/median/variance, skew, Bayes' theorem, hypothesis tests
Linear algebra & calculus basics: vectors, dot products, matrix multiplication, derivatives and gradients
Exploratory data analysis with Matplotlib/Seaborn: histograms, scatter plots, box plots, correlations

steps.title: Classical Machine Learning
steps.subtitle: Train, evaluate and tune models with scikit-learn
steps.description: Learn the core algorithms asked in every ML interview and, just as important, how to evaluate them honestly. You will build scikit-learn pipelines, pick the right metric, validate with cross-validation and diagnose overfitting versus underfitting.

topics.name: Supervised learning: linear & logistic regression, k-NN, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting
Unsupervised learning: k-means clustering and PCA for dimensionality reduction
Feature engineering with scikit-learn Pipeline / ColumnTransformer (fit on training data only)
Evaluation metrics: confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, MAE/RMSE, calibration
Train/validation/test splits, k-fold, stratified and grouped cross-validation, data leakage
Bias-variance trade-off, overfitting vs underfitting and L1/L2 regularization
Hyperparameter tuning (GridSearchCV/RandomizedSearchCV) and handling imbalanced classes

steps.title: Deep Learning
steps.subtitle: Build and train neural networks in PyTorch
steps.description: Understand how neural networks learn, from activation functions and backpropagation to optimizers, and train them yourself in PyTorch (or TensorFlow/Keras). You will build CNNs for images and LSTMs for sequences, and learn the techniques that stop deep models from overfitting.

topics.name: Neural network basics: neurons, layers, activations (ReLU, sigmoid, softmax) and loss functions
Backpropagation and gradient descent: chain rule, learning rate, mini-batches and epochs
PyTorch essentials: tensors, autograd, Dataset/DataLoader, the training loop, model.train()/model.eval()
Optimization: SGD with momentum, Adam, learning-rate schedules and batch normalization
Overfitting control: dropout, weight decay, early stopping and data augmentation
CNNs for images: convolution, pooling, output shapes and transfer learning
Sequence models: RNN, LSTM/GRU and the vanishing-gradient problem

steps.title: NLP, LLMs & MLOps
steps.subtitle: Ship language models and ML services to production
steps.description: Move from notebooks to products: work with text using Transformers and embeddings, build a simple retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) app, then serve models behind a FastAPI service in Docker, track experiments with MLflow and monitor deployed models for drift.

topics.name: Text preprocessing and representation: tokenization (subword/BPE), TF-IDF and word embeddings
Transformers: self-attention, BERT vs GPT and fine-tuning with Hugging Face
LLM apps: prompting, sentence embeddings, vector search and RAG basics
Model serving: a REST API with FastAPI, containerized with Docker
Experiment tracking and model registry with MLflow
Production monitoring: latency, data drift, concept drift and retraining triggers
